:::{#exm-pois-two-group-mle}
#### Estimating a rate ratio from two cohorts

An unexposed cohort contributes $D_0 = 12$ events
over $T_0 = 4000$ person-years,
and an exposed cohort contributes $D_1 = 15$ events
over $T_1 = 2500$ person-years.
By @thm-pois-two-group-mle,
the Poisson regression estimates are:

$$
\ba
\el(0)
&= \frac{D_0}{T_0}
&& \text{(crude rate, unexposed)} \\
&= \frac{12}{4000}
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= 0.003
&& \text{(divide)} \\
\el(1)
&= \frac{D_1}{T_1}
&& \text{(crude rate, exposed)} \\
&= \frac{15}{2500}
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= 0.006
&& \text{(divide)} \\
\erateratio(1 : 0)
&= \frac{0.006}{0.003}
&& \text{(ratio of crude rates)} \\
&= 2
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

so $\eb_0 = \logf{0.003} \approx -5.809$
and $\eb_1 = \logf{2} \approx 0.693$.
Fitting the same model in R
(with $\logf{t_i}$ as an [offset](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-offset))
gives the same estimates:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
two_cohorts <- data.frame(
  exposed = c(0, 1),
  events = c(12, 15),
  person_years = c(4000, 2500)
)
fit_two_cohorts <- glm(
  events ~ exposed + offset(log(person_years)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = two_cohorts
)
coef(fit_two_cohorts)
exp(coef(fit_two_cohorts))
```

:::
